pathway.title: Core & Main, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Business risk is moderate: customers are highly diversified and capital needs are low, but demand follows construction. Tens of thousands of customers buy from the company, the top 50 are about 10% of net sales and the largest is under 1%; capital expenditure was 0.47% of net sales in fiscal 2024; and fiscal 2024 net sales of USD 7,441 million are 19.08% of a USD 39 billion market that management estimates. Against that, about 58% of sales go to private non-residential and residential construction on management's estimates, and the first half of fiscal 2026 sales grew only 1.27%, mainly through acquisitions. Basis: calculation CX1; calculation MS1; calculation NM1; calculation GR2; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8, 14, 15, 86, 87; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 33; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Earnings have been flat while debt grew, which is why leverage is the issue. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 935 million in fiscal 2022, USD 910 million in fiscal 2023 and USD 930 million in fiscal 2024, a fall of 0.53% over two years, although the Adjusted EBITDA margin fell from 13.58% to 12.50% as SG&A rose 15.79% in fiscal 2024 against sales growth of 11.03%. Net debt rose from USD 1,877 million to USD 2,253 million in that year, taking net debt to reported EBITDA from 2.11x to 2.49x and cash interest cover from 8.47x to 4.59x. Basis: calculation EB1; calculation EM1; calculation EM2; calculation GR1; calculation GR3; calculation ND1; calculation ND2; calculation LV1; calculation LV2; calculation CV1; calculation CV2; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 86, 97, 108; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Cash conversion is the main operating support, but it is seasonal and uneven. Operating cash flow was 117.47% of Adjusted EBITDA in fiscal 2023 and 66.77% in fiscal 2024, and 28.80% in the first half of fiscal 2026 against 22.65%, because working capital absorbed USD 242 million in that half. The company says cash flow is typically lower in the first two quarters and higher in the last two, and its fiscal 2026 outlook of operating cash flow at 60% to 70% of Adjusted EBITDA implies second-half operating cash flow of USD 426 million to USD 542 million. Basis: calculation CN1; calculation CN2; calculation CN3; calculation CN4; calculation WC1; calculation GL6; calculation GL7; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5

Liquidity is strong and refinancing risk is low until 2031. Liquidity was USD 1,538 million at August 2, 2026, before USD 11 million of repurchases made after that date: cash plus USD 1,226 million of availability on an undrawn USD 1,250 million revolver, which depends on the borrowing base. Debt payments and tax receivable payments due within 12 months are only USD 58 million, and liquidity is 6.36x the working capital outflow of the first half. The first final maturity is February 2031, and the 2031 loan, the 2033 loan and the 2034 notes are 37.45%, 32.28% and 30.27% of principal; the notes' fair value is 99.60% of par, which shows market access after the July 2026 refinancing. Basis: calculation LQ1; calculation LQ2; calculation LQ3; calculation LQ5; calculation WC1; calculation DS2; calculation DS3; calculation DS4; calculation DS14; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 18, 20, 36; EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Leverage is moderate on the last measurable basis and rising in absolute terms. Net debt was USD 1,928 million at the end of fiscal 2025 and USD 2,137 million at August 2, 2026, USD 2,148 million pro forma for USD 11 million of repurchases after that date, which is 2.19x to 2.26x the fiscal 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance of USD 950 million to USD 980 million. That is an indicator on company guidance, not a trailing ratio, and the August balance is seasonally high; six-month Adjusted EBITDA covered six-month interest expense 8.47x against 8.03x a year earlier, but covered cash interest paid 8.47x against 10.00x. Basis: calculation ND3; calculation ND4; calculation PF1; calculation GL1; calculation GL3; calculation HC1; calculation HC2; calculation HC3; calculation HC4; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8, 42; EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5

Financial policy is the weakest dimension. In the first half of fiscal 2026 the company repurchased USD 257 million of shares and paid USD 42 million under the tax receivable agreements, USD 299 million against free cash flow of USD 112 million, and net new debt was USD 293 million; USD 412 million of a USD 1 billion repurchase authorization was unused at August 2, 2026. Claims outside debt, lease liabilities and the tax receivable payable, add USD 985 million, 46.09% of net debt, and the payable can accelerate on a change of control. Basis: calculation SR1; calculation FC4; calculation SR3; calculation OC3; calculation OC4; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8, 10, 20

The primary downside path is a construction downturn met with unchanged shareholder returns. Each 1 percentage point of gross margin is worth USD 40.55 million of six-month gross profit, 8.11% of six-month Adjusted EBITDA, and each 1% fall in six-month sales removes USD 10.93 million, 2.19% of that EBITDA, if SG&A does not fall; in fiscal 2024 SG&A rose faster than sales and operating income fell 2.84%. Variable-rate debt is 69.73% of principal and the swap covers 86.81% of it only to July 2028, after which each 1 percentage point costs USD 17.28 million a year. Basis: calculation SN1; calculation SN2; calculation SN3; calculation SN4; calculation GR4; calculation DS8; calculation DS9; calculation DS12; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 33

runs.text: The strongest support is liquidity and maturity profile: USD 1,538 million of liquidity on an undrawn revolver and a first final maturity in February 2031 mean that seasonal working capital and debt service can be met without market access for several years, so refinancing risk is low before fiscal 2030. Basis: calculation LQ1; calculation LQ5; calculation DS5; calculation DS6; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 19, 36; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The second support is a broad customer base with low capital needs: no customer is above 1% of net sales, the top 50 are about 10% and capital expenditure is 0.47% of net sales, so cash flow does not depend on a single account or on heavy reinvestment. Basis: calculation CX1; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 86, 108

The third support is a stable gross margin of 26.61% to 27.13% across periods, which together with pass-through pricing limits margin shocks from supplier cost changes. Basis: calculation GM1; calculation GM2; calculation GM3; calculation GM4; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 33

The fourth support is demonstrated market access on improving terms: three term loan repricings since May 2024 and a July 2026 refinancing that raised USD 1,550 million of new debt, with fair values of 99.60% of par for the notes, 99.75% for the 2033 loan and 100.00% for the 2031 loan. Basis: calculation RF1; calculation DS14; calculation DS15; calculation DS16; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 17, 18; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The fifth support is the absence of a controlling holder, a dividend or a creditor-adverse transaction in the documents supplied, which removes sponsor extraction as a driver. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)

The main weakness is financial policy: USD 299 million of repurchases and tax receivable payments in the first half of fiscal 2026 exceeded free cash flow of USD 112 million by USD 187 million and net new debt was USD 293 million, so leverage rises unless EBITDA grows or repurchases slow. Basis: calculation SR1; calculation FC4; calculation SR2; calculation SR3; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 8; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The second weakness is that leverage is not measurable on a trailing basis and has risen: net debt to reported EBITDA went from 2.11x to 2.49x in fiscal 2024 and cash interest cover from 8.47x to 4.59x, and no later ratio is stated. Basis: calculation LV1; calculation LV2; calculation CV1; calculation CV2; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The third weakness is operating leverage in a construction-linked business: SG&A grew 15.79% against sales growth of 11.03% in fiscal 2024 and Adjusted EBITDA has been flat since fiscal 2022, so a volume decline would reach cash flow faster than costs fall. Basis: calculation GR1; calculation GR3; calculation EB1; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 86, 97

The fourth weakness is claims outside debt: USD 985 million of lease liabilities and tax receivable payable, 46.09% of net debt, with the tax receivable payable accelerating on a change of control. Basis: calculation OC1; calculation OC2; calculation OC3; calculation OC4; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 20

The fifth weakness is rate exposure: 69.73% of principal is variable-rate, the swap covers 86.81% of it only to July 2028, and each 1 percentage point on all variable-rate debt would cost USD 17.28 million a year after that. Basis: calculation DS7; calculation DS8; calculation DS9; calculation DS12; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 28

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The latest financing closed on July 1, 2026, when a new USD 800 million term loan due 2033 and USD 750 million of 6.0% unsecured notes due 2034 repaid the term loan due 2028. Debt principal rose by USD 318 million in the second quarter, and USD 320 million of the new borrowing exceeded the balance of the old loan; the offering notice names general corporate purposes including acquisitions and share repurchases, and the quarterly report does not say how the excess was used. Basis: calculation RF1; calculation RF3; calculation RF5; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 18; EX99.1_2026-05-03_cnm_jun2026seniornoteslaunchpr-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1

Earlier steps moved maturities out in stages: a USD 750 million term loan due 2031 in February 2024, an increase of USD 200 million in December 2024, a revolver extended to 2031 in April 2026 and a margin cut on the 2031 loan from 2.00% to 1.75% in August 2026. The revolver was undrawn at August 2, 2026 and the company states compliance with all debt covenants at that date. Basis: 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 79, 128; 10-Q_2026-05-03_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 19, 23
No debt issue after August 2026, no third-quarter report and no credit rating action are supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The supplied filings support a credit snapshot of Core & Main, Inc. as at the second quarter of fiscal 2026, but not a trailing twelve-month leverage figure, because the annual report for the year ended February 1, 2026 is missing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The latest balance sheet is dated 108 days before the as-of date and no third-quarter material is supplied. The executed credit agreements, the indenture for the 2034 notes and their amendments are also absent, so covenant, guarantee and security conclusions can rest only on the quarterly report's own summaries. No credit rating level or market price is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For creditors, net debt, cash and revolver availability at the end of the second quarter can be read directly from the filings, while leverage and coverage have to be shown on six-month results or company guidance and labelled as such.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Material gap: the annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended February 1, 2026 and the results release for that year are not supplied. Both quarterly reports refer to that annual report and carry its year-end balance sheet as a comparative, but no annual income statement, cash flow statement or Adjusted EBITDA for fiscal 2025 appears in any supplied document, and a search of every source for fiscal 2025, trailing and twelve-month figures found none. Trailing twelve-month leverage, coverage and cash conversion are therefore not calculable, and fiscal 2025 comparisons are limited to the balance sheet. The minimum remedy is that annual report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Material gap: no executed financing document is supplied. The term loan credit agreement with its sixth and seventh amendments, the asset-based credit agreement with its latest amendment, and the indenture and first supplemental indenture for the 2034 notes appear only as exhibit references, and the run settings state that no legal documents were supplied. Covenant definitions, guarantor and security terms and the exact repricing terms can therefore be read only from the filings' own summaries. The minimum remedy is those agreements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Minor gap: no third-quarter material is supplied. The latest balance sheet is dated August 2, 2026 and the latest document September 9, 2026, while the third quarter of fiscal 2026 ends on November 1, 2026 on the company's 13-week calendar, so any later financing, repurchase or trading change is not visible.

fields.value: Financial foundation for Core & Main, Inc. (issuer id cnm-1856525), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the issuer's income statement, cash flow statement, balance sheet, debt and liquidity, with calculated leverage and cover ratios where the sources allow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt of USD 2,449 million is backed by USD 1,538 million of cash and revolver availability, but leverage and interest cover can be stated only for fiscal 2023 and 2024, because the annual report for the year ended February 1, 2026 is missing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation TD5; calculation LQ1; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On balance-sheet carrying value, net debt was USD 2,137 million at August 2, 2026, below USD 2,253 million at the end of fiscal 2024, when it was 2.49x reported EBITDA, even though the company repurchased USD 257 million of shares in the first half of fiscal 2026 and raised USD 293 million of net new debt. A further USD 11 million of repurchases after the quarter end lifts pro forma net debt to USD 2,148 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation ND5; calculation ND2; calculation LV2; calculation DF1; calculation PB1; EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 8.47x in fiscal 2023 and 4.59x in fiscal 2024; no later cover ratio can be stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt on carrying value rose from USD 1,877 million at the end of fiscal 2023 to USD 2,253 million at the end of fiscal 2024, taking net debt to reported EBITDA from 2.11x to 2.49x, because acquisitions of USD 741 million and share repurchases of USD 176 million were funded beside operating cash flow of USD 621 million. Net debt then fell to USD 1,928 million at the end of fiscal 2025 and rose by USD 209 million to USD 2,137 million by August 2, 2026, as USD 257 million of share repurchases and USD 42 million of tax receivable agreement payments outweighed free cash flow of USD 112 million. The direction since fiscal 2024 is lower, but no ratio can be stated for the later dates.

fields.value: Basis: calculation ND1; calculation ND2; calculation ND3; calculation ND5; calculation NC1; calculation NC3; calculation FC4; calculation LV1; calculation LV2; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 4.59x in fiscal 2024 against 8.47x in fiscal 2023, because interest expense rose from USD 81 million to USD 142 million after the acquisitions and larger borrowings, and cash interest paid rose from USD 105 million to USD 197 million. In the first half of fiscal 2026 cash interest paid was USD 59 million against USD 49 million while interest expense eased from USD 61 million to USD 59 million; without trailing twelve-month EBITDA the current cover ratio is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CV1; calculation CV2; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 106, 108; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity at August 2, 2026 was USD 1,538 million: USD 312 million of cash and about USD 1,226 million of availability under the undrawn USD 1,250 million revolver, which depends on the borrowing base; an April 2026 amendment extended its maturity from 2029 to 2031. The July 2026 refinancing replaced the 2028 term loan with a USD 800 million term loan due 2033 and USD 750 million of senior notes due 2034, so scheduled principal is only USD 17 million a year until the USD 928 million term loan falls due in 2031.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow was USD 144 million in the first half of fiscal 2026 against USD 111 million, after working capital absorbed USD 242 million (USD 255 million a year earlier), and free cash flow after USD 32 million of capital expenditure was USD 112 million. Share repurchases and tax receivable agreement payments of USD 299 million exceeded that by USD 187 million, and net new debt of USD 293 million covered the gap, so shareholder returns in the half were partly debt-funded.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation FC4; calculation FC3; calculation WC1; calculation WC2; calculation SR1; calculation SR2; calculation DF1; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Outside debt, the balance sheet carries USD 644 million of tax receivable agreement liabilities, whose cash payments were USD 42 million in the first half against USD 18 million, USD 300 million of operating lease liabilities and USD 1,223 million of supplier purchase obligations that are generally cancellable; none is in the debt or net debt figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA are the issuer's own figures, with add-backs of USD 25 million in fiscal 2024, so the choice of measure moves net leverage by only 0.07x; depreciation and amortization is stated as USD 183 million, USD 186 million and USD 194 million on three bases in fiscal 2024, and fiscal 2024 had 53 weeks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation AB1; calculation LV2; calculation LV3; calculation LV4; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 78, 97, 106, 108

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against reading the lower net debt as deleveraging is seasonality and funding: working capital absorbed USD 242 million in the half and part of the repurchases was debt-funded, so the year-end balance for fiscal 2026 could look different from the August balance. The case for stability is that the revolver was undrawn at August 2, 2026 and at the end of fiscal 2025, and the earliest bullet maturity is in 2031. A fiscal 2025 annual report showing EBITDA far below the USD 905 million of fiscal 2024, or third-quarter results showing net debt staying near USD 2,137 million after the seasonal working capital outflow reverses, would change the view.

fields.value: - High severity: The annual statements for fiscal 2025 (the year ended February 1, 2026) are not supplied, so the income statement and cash flow columns for fiscal 2025 are absent, no trailing twelve-month EBITDA, cash interest, revenue or operating cash flow can be built, and leverage and interest cover at fiscal 2025 and at August 2, 2026 are not calculable. The action that would close it is the annual report for that year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium severity: Lines that the statements print only in some periods, or print as a dash, are shown as not supplied in the other periods and are not read as zero: other expense, acquisitions, investment in tax advantaged limited partnerships, borrowings and repayments on the revolver, issuance of long-term debt, debt issuance costs, and other investing and financing items. This restricts nothing beyond those lines, because the totals tie, and no action is needed beyond reading the dash as not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium severity: Revolver availability and letters of credit at February 1, 2026 are not stated, so undrawn committed facilities for fiscal 2025 are not supplied, and the principal debt at that date is not stated. The action that would close it is the annual report for the year ended February 1, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium severity: Cumulative leverage in the debt stack is not supplied for any facility because no trailing twelve-month EBITDA denominator exists; the amounts and ranks are stated. The action that would close it is the fiscal 2025 annual report, which would allow a trailing twelve-month figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium severity: The cash flow statement shows issuance of long-term debt of USD 929 million and repayments of USD 617 million in the six months ended August 2, 2026, which are not the new USD 800 million term loan and USD 750 million of notes, and the quarterly report does not reconcile them; the net change in principal ties but the gross flows should not be read as instrument amounts. The action that would close it is the issuer's reconciliation of the refinancing, which the executed amendment and indenture would give.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium severity: Carrying values by instrument are not disclosed in the quarterly report, so the net unamortized discount and issuance costs of USD 29 million at August 2, 2026 is derived as carrying value less principal; it restricts the instrument-level carrying values, which are not supplied. The action that would close it is the debt note of the annual report for the year ended February 1, 2026 or the third-quarter report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low severity: Maintenance and growth capital expenditure are not disclosed, so only total capital expenditure is used in free cash flow; interest income, exceptional items, restricted cash, finance lease liabilities, supplier finance arrangements and a separate second-quarter cash flow statement are not presented in the statements and notes searched, so none is stated and the second-quarter cash flow columns are omitted. No action closes this from the issuer's public statements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low severity: The lien priority between the revolving facility and the term loans, and the guarantors of the credit facilities, are not stated in the supplied filings, so the debt stack ranks secured debt together and the unsecured notes behind it without a ranking between the secured facilities. The action that would close it is the credit agreements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low severity: The repricing of the 2031 Senior Term Loan is dated only as August 2026 in the subsequent-events note and the repurchases after quarter end carry no day, so the post-balance-sheet rows state no day and no principal effect for the repricing. The action that would close it is the third-quarter report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low severity: The company reports one operating segment and no corporate or eliminations line, so no segment sum is stated beyond the product-category net sales, whose meter category is reported as smart utility products in the 2026 documents without a stated link between them. The action that would close it is the issuer's own mapping of the two labels.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low severity: The covenant ratio that governs excess cash flow repayment, a secured leverage ratio of 3.25 or more, and the fixed charge coverage test are defined in agreements that are not supplied and no reported covenant figure is stated, although the quarterly report states compliance with all debt covenants at August 2, 2026, so covenant capacity is not inferred. The action that would close it is the credit agreements and the issuer's reported covenant figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business & governance for Core & Main, Inc. (issuer id cnm-1856525), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the issuer's business and operating model, ownership and control, transaction and financing history, and the sponsor and governance behaviour that bears on creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor and governance risk for creditors is medium: the former sponsor has held no shares since January 2024, but the company has funded sponsor-exit repurchases, acquisitions and growing buybacks partly from borrowings, and the covenants that would cap this are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation SE4; calculation CR4; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating base is diversified, with no customer above 1% of net sales in fiscal 2024, so the governance structure drives this view. Creditors face a recurring cash claim from the tax receivable agreements: USD 685 million is owed to former owners and the management holding vehicle, with USD 41 million expected within 12 months. In the second quarter of fiscal 2026 debt principal rose USD 318 million while the company repurchased USD 169 million of shares.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation TR1; calculation RF5; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 20; EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor controls Core & Main, so no sponsor-driven distribution or sponsor equity support is documented in either direction. CD&R, the former sponsor, sold down through secondary offerings, seven of them between April 2023 and January 2024, and held no Class A or Class B shares from January 25, 2024. The company bought 28.05% of the shares those sellers disposed of in fiscal 2023, for USD 1,344 million. What remains is a classified board, Class A shares that are in many cases held through brokers and institutions (three holders of record at February 2, 2025) and the management holding vehicle's 3.30% of the combined Class A and Class B shares, held as Class B; larger current holders are not established because the proxy statement is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation SE1; calculation SE2; calculation SE3; calculation SE4; calculation OW5; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 68, 75, 110

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sponsor exit was financed partly with borrowings, and it is the clearest case of cash going to shareholders while debt rose. In fiscal 2023, the year of the USD 1,344 million repurchases, net borrowings on the revolver rose USD 430 million and cash fell USD 176 million. A new USD 750 million term loan on February 9, 2024 repaid that revolver balance and named share repurchases among its permitted uses, so the exit financing became term debt; the revolver stood at USD 93 million at February 2, 2025 and was undrawn at February 1, 2026 and August 2, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation SE4; calculation SE5; calculation SE6; 10-K_2024-01-28_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 96, 113, 135; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 79, 127; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns have grown and now exceed free cash flow, so leverage depends on earnings growth rather than debt paydown. In the first half of fiscal 2026 the company repurchased USD 257 million of shares and paid USD 42 million under the tax receivable agreements, USD 299 million in all against free cash flow of USD 112 million, while net new debt was USD 293 million. The authorization is USD 1 billion with USD 412 million unused at August 2, 2026, and a further USD 11 million was repurchased after the quarter end, so the pattern can continue. In fiscal 2024 acquisition spending was 4.21x repurchases of USD 176 million; in the first half of fiscal 2026 there were no acquisitions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The July 2026 refinancing lengthened maturities but raised debt principal. A USD 800 million term loan due 2033 and USD 750 million of 6.0% unsecured notes due 2034 repaid the term loan due 2028, so the first term maturity is now 2031. Debt principal rose USD 318 million in the second quarter and USD 320 million of the new borrowing exceeded the balance repaid; the offering notice named acquisitions and share repurchases among the uses and the quarterly report does not say how the excess was used. The notes rank equally in right of payment with other senior debt, while substantially all assets of the borrower secure the term loans and the revolver.

fields.value: Basis: calculation RF1; calculation RF2; calculation RF3; calculation RF4; calculation RF5; calculation RF6; 10-Q_2026-05-03_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 16, 18, 19; EX99.1_2026-05-03_cnm_jun2026seniornoteslaunchpr-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tax receivable agreements are the largest related-party claim and the main change-of-control exposure. USD 685 million was owed at August 2, 2026, USD 35 million less than the USD 720 million at February 1, 2026, with USD 41 million expected within 12 months; the payments do not depend on holders keeping their shares. Each agreement can accelerate on a change of control, a prolonged payment default or an early termination, and the CD&R investors' consent may be needed to refinance debt on terms more restrictive on those payments. The amount payable on acceleration is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation TR1; calculation TR2; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 56, 60, 61; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisitions drove past growth and were funded with cash and term loan borrowings, but have paused. Ten acquisitions with USD 769 million of transaction value closed in fiscal 2024 and two with USD 76 million in fiscal 2025, and none closed in the first half of fiscal 2026. Sales grew 1.27% in that half and the quarterly report attributes the increase mainly to acquisitions, so organic growth, including seven greenfield locations opened in fiscal 2026, has not yet replaced purchased volume.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation AQ1; calculation OP1; calculation OP7; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 122; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 33; EX99.1_2026-05-03_cnm_cnmq12026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The customer base is highly diversified, but sales are concentrated in one product family and in construction-linked end markets. No customer exceeds 1% of net sales and the top 50 are about 10%; pipes, valves and fittings were 67.28% of fiscal 2024 sales; non-municipal end markets were about 58% of sales on management's estimates; and the first half of fiscal 2026 absorbed USD 242 million of working capital. Gross profit was 27.0% of net sales in that half against 26.7%, so the margin cushion is steady.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation MX1; calculation EM1; calculation OP4; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 9, 14; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure supports monitoring of reported facts: the latest audited accounts carry opinions without qualification and effective internal control over financial reporting, and the quarterly report states covenant compliance at August 2, 2026. What lenders cannot see in the documents supplied is the covenant calculation itself or the restricted-payment capacity behind it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for lower risk is that the structure has been handled prudently: the company has no approved dividend plan, the revolver was undrawn at February 1, 2026 and August 2, 2026, three term loan repricings since May 2024 have cut the margin, final maturities now start in 2031, and the quarterly report states compliance with all debt covenants. If fiscal 2026 buybacks and tax receivable payments are met from operating cash flow rather than new term debt and the next annual report shows principal falling, the view would move to low. It would move to high if a new controlling holder appears, if the credit agreements show wide restricted-payment capacity that the company uses for larger debt-funded buybacks, if tax receivable payments accelerate, or if any amendment subordinates or releases lenders.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so current holders above 5%, board composition and committee membership are not established, and the conclusion that no holder controls the company rests on share counts and on the annual and quarterly reports naming none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreements and the notes indenture are not supplied, so the restricted-payment and debt-incurrence capacity that decides whether the buyback pattern can widen is not measured, and the medium risk level cannot be moved up or down on capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The tax receivable agreements are not supplied, so the sum payable on acceleration after a change of control is not established; only the recorded payable of USD 685 million is known.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The annual report for the year ended February 1, 2026 is not supplied, so the date the repurchase authorization rose to USD 1 billion and the fiscal 2025 buyback total are not reported; fiscal 2025 buybacks of about USD 155 million are derived, not stated.

fields.value: - Class B voting rights, whether the 2021 Stockholders Agreement with CD&R still applies after its exit, and any fees paid to the former sponsor are not stated in the documents supplied, so freedom from sponsor-related leakage beyond the tax receivable agreements is not confirmed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The level is driven by debt-funded shareholder returns and the tax receivable claim, because they move cash from the operating group to shareholders and former owners, which implies that leverage depends on earnings growth. Countervailing evidence is the absence of a controlling holder, dividends or creditor-adverse transactions. Further analysis requires the credit agreements, the tax receivable agreements and the proxy statement.

fields.value: The latest financing closed on July 1, 2026, when a new USD 800 million term loan due 2033 and USD 750 million of 6.0% unsecured notes due 2034 repaid the term loan due 2028. Debt principal rose by USD 318 million in the second quarter, and USD 320 million of the new borrowing exceeded the balance of the old loan; the offering notice names general corporate purposes including acquisitions and share repurchases, and the quarterly report does not say how the excess was used.

fields.value: Earlier steps moved maturities out in stages: a USD 750 million term loan due 2031 in February 2024, an increase of USD 200 million in December 2024, a revolver extended to 2031 in April 2026 and a margin cut on the 2031 loan from 2.00% to 1.75% in August 2026. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit for Core & Main, Inc. (issuer id cnm-1856525), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the integrated fundamental credit view: business and operating model, financial profile, liquidity and refinancing, financial policy, downside path and monitoring triggers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Core & Main's fundamental credit is adequate: USD 1,538 million of liquidity and no final maturity before 2031 support it, but shareholder returns now exceed free cash flow, so the creditor risk is leverage drift, not near-term liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation LQ1; calculation SR1; calculation FC4; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the last measurable basis net debt was 2.49x reported EBITDA at the end of fiscal 2024, and EBITDA covered cash interest 4.59x; the annual report for the year ended February 1, 2026 is missing, so trailing leverage cannot be stated. Net debt was USD 2,137 million at August 2, 2026 and USD 2,148 million pro forma for USD 11 million of repurchases made after that date, on a day the report does not state, about 2.23x the midpoint of the company's fiscal 2026 EBITDA guidance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation LV2; calculation CV2; calculation ND4; calculation PF1; calculation GL2; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business risk is moderate: customers are highly diversified and capital needs are low, but demand follows construction. Tens of thousands of customers buy from the company, the top 50 are about 10% of net sales and the largest is under 1%; capital expenditure was 0.47% of net sales in fiscal 2024; and fiscal 2024 net sales of USD 7,441 million are 19.08% of a USD 39 billion market that management estimates. Against that, about 58% of sales go to private non-residential and residential construction on management's estimates, and the first half of fiscal 2026 sales grew only 1.27%, mainly through acquisitions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CX1; calculation MS1; calculation NM1; calculation GR2; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8, 14, 15, 86, 87; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 33; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings have been flat while debt grew, which is why leverage is the issue. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 935 million in fiscal 2022, USD 910 million in fiscal 2023 and USD 930 million in fiscal 2024, a fall of 0.53% over two years, although the Adjusted EBITDA margin fell from 13.58% to 12.50% as SG&A rose 15.79% in fiscal 2024 against sales growth of 11.03%. Net debt rose from USD 1,877 million to USD 2,253 million in that year, taking net debt to reported EBITDA from 2.11x to 2.49x and cash interest cover from 8.47x to 4.59x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation EB1; calculation EM1; calculation EM2; calculation GR1; calculation GR3; calculation ND1; calculation ND2; calculation LV1; calculation LV2; calculation CV1; calculation CV2; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 86, 97, 108; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is the main operating support, but it is seasonal and uneven. Operating cash flow was 117.47% of Adjusted EBITDA in fiscal 2023 and 66.77% in fiscal 2024, and 28.80% in the first half of fiscal 2026 against 22.65%, because working capital absorbed USD 242 million in that half. The company says cash flow is typically lower in the first two quarters and higher in the last two, and its fiscal 2026 outlook of operating cash flow at 60% to 70% of Adjusted EBITDA implies second-half operating cash flow of USD 426 million to USD 542 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CN1; calculation CN2; calculation CN3; calculation CN4; calculation WC1; calculation GL6; calculation GL7; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is strong and refinancing risk is low until 2031. Liquidity was USD 1,538 million at August 2, 2026, before USD 11 million of repurchases made after that date: cash plus USD 1,226 million of availability on an undrawn USD 1,250 million revolver, which depends on the borrowing base. Debt payments and tax receivable payments due within 12 months are only USD 58 million, and liquidity is 6.36x the working capital outflow of the first half. The first final maturity is February 2031, and the 2031 loan, the 2033 loan and the 2034 notes are 37.45%, 32.28% and 30.27% of principal; the notes' fair value is 99.60% of par, which shows market access after the July 2026 refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation LQ1; calculation LQ2; calculation LQ3; calculation LQ5; calculation WC1; calculation DS2; calculation DS3; calculation DS4; calculation DS14; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 18, 20, 36; EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is moderate on the last measurable basis and rising in absolute terms. Net debt was USD 1,928 million at the end of fiscal 2025 and USD 2,137 million at August 2, 2026, USD 2,148 million pro forma for USD 11 million of repurchases after that date, which is 2.19x to 2.26x the fiscal 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance of USD 950 million to USD 980 million. That is an indicator on company guidance, not a trailing ratio, and the August balance is seasonally high; six-month Adjusted EBITDA covered six-month interest expense 8.47x against 8.03x a year earlier, but covered cash interest paid 8.47x against 10.00x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation ND3; calculation ND4; calculation PF1; calculation GL1; calculation GL3; calculation HC1; calculation HC2; calculation HC3; calculation HC4; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8, 42; EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the weakest dimension. In the first half of fiscal 2026 the company repurchased USD 257 million of shares and paid USD 42 million under the tax receivable agreements, USD 299 million against free cash flow of USD 112 million, and net new debt was USD 293 million; USD 412 million of a USD 1 billion repurchase authorization was unused at August 2, 2026. Claims outside debt, lease liabilities and the tax receivable payable, add USD 985 million, 46.09% of net debt, and the payable can accelerate on a change of control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation SR1; calculation FC4; calculation SR3; calculation OC3; calculation OC4; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8, 10, 20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path is a construction downturn met with unchanged shareholder returns. Each 1 percentage point of gross margin is worth USD 40.55 million of six-month gross profit, 8.11% of six-month Adjusted EBITDA, and each 1% fall in six-month sales removes USD 10.93 million, 2.19% of that EBITDA, if SG&A does not fall; in fiscal 2024 SG&A rose faster than sales and operating income fell 2.84%. Variable-rate debt is 69.73% of principal and the swap covers 86.81% of it only to July 2028, after which each 1 percentage point costs USD 17.28 million a year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation SN1; calculation SN2; calculation SN3; calculation SN4; calculation GR4; calculation DS8; calculation DS9; calculation DS12; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is that the company can delever quickly when it chooses: net debt fell USD 325 million in fiscal 2025 while it still repurchased shares, free cash flow was USD 1,030 million in fiscal 2023, the revolver is undrawn, and buybacks, acquisitions and the pace of greenfield openings are discretionary. If the third-quarter report and the annual report for fiscal 2025 show trailing net debt to EBITDA at or below about 2.23x and buybacks met from operating cash flow, the view would move up. It would move down if net debt rises through the seasonally stronger second half, if Adjusted EBITDA falls below the fiscal 2024 level of USD 930 million, if the revolver is drawn to fund repurchases, or if a larger acquisition is financed with debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation NC3; calculation FC1; calculation GL2; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 97, 108; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 18; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The conclusion that leverage is moderate rests on the fiscal 2024 ratio and on a guidance-based indicator, and it would change if the missing fiscal 2025 results show EBITDA far below fiscal 2024 or year-end net debt well above the August balance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreements and the borrowing base are not supplied, so the strong liquidity conclusion holds only if the borrowing base supports the stated availability, and a downturn that shrinks receivables and inventory would lower it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No credit rating, market spread or peer set is supplied, so the adequate judgement is absolute and not relative to other leveraged issuers, and the pricing of the credit cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The fiscal 2026 outlook is management's own and unaudited, so the guidance-based leverage indicator and the implied second-half cash flow would move with any miss, and a miss in the second half is the case that would break the leverage drift conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The split of sales by end market and the product category labels come from fiscal 2024 management estimates and from a category renamed in 2026, so the cyclical share of about 58% may have moved and the construction exposure conclusion is bounded.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Core & Main distributes water, wastewater, storm drainage and fire protection products and related services to municipalities, private water companies and professional contractors through over 370 branches in the United States and Canada, selling more than 225,000 products from more than 5,000 suppliers to more than 60,000 customers. Fiscal 2024 net sales of USD 7,441 million are 19.08% of a USD 39 billion addressable market that management estimates, and the company names one other national competitor. The model earns about 27% of sales as gross profit by buying at scale and passing product costs to customers with a lag, and it links cash flow to repair and replacement of water infrastructure, to private construction and, for fire protection, to building projects; the business grew through acquisitions after a lineage that began in 1874 and a CD&R ownership from 2017 to January 2024.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation MS1; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 7, 15, 86; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 29; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For creditors the customer base supports cash-flow visibility, because no customer is above 1% of net sales and the top 50 are about 10%, and low capital needs (0.47% of net sales in fiscal 2024) help liquidity preservation. Revenue is not contracted, so debt service depends on construction activity and on the second-half release of working capital rather than on committed revenue, and refinancing confidence rests on the market access shown in July 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CX1; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 18; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Core & Main, Inc. is a listed holding company whose main asset is its interest in Core & Main Holdings, LP, which sits above the borrower, Core & Main LP. No holder is identified as controlling: CD&R, the owner from 2017, held no shares after January 25, 2024, the company repurchased USD 1,344 million of shares and interests from CD&R-affiliated sellers in fiscal 2023, and the management holding vehicle holds a non-controlling interest of 3.3%. The 2034 notes are guaranteed by the borrower's parent companies, while the term loans and the revolver are secured on substantially all assets of the borrower, so the structural exposure is to the group, not to a controlling holder.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 21, 80, 110; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 18, 19, 22; EX99.1_2026-05-03_cnm_jun2026seniornoteslaunchpr-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The structural points for creditors are the USD 685 million tax receivable payable to former owners and management, which the listed company pays out of distributions from the operating partnership and which can accelerate on a change of control, and a consent point for the CD&R investors on refinancing terms that are more restrictive on those payments. Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk Medium, and this module agrees: the risk comes from debt-funded shareholder returns and the tax receivable claim, not from sponsor control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation OC2; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 56, 60, 61; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sales follow municipal repair and replacement (about 42% of fiscal 2024 sales on management's estimate), private non-residential and residential construction (about 38% and 20%) and acquisitions: the first half of fiscal 2026 grew 1.27% mainly through acquisitions, storm drainage fell 2.9% on lower volume and fire protection rose 15.3% on volume and price. The first quarter was flat because lower volume was offset by acquisitions, and fire protection net sales fell 13.37% in fiscal 2024, so category risk is real even though the base is broad. Revenue is repeat but transactional: no contract length, renewal or churn data is supplied, and switching costs are not quantified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation GR2; calculation GR5; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8, 86; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 31, 33; EX99.1_2026-05-03_cnm_cnmq12026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Pricing is passed through with a lag as product costs move: the 27.1% gross margin of fiscal 2023 benefited from inventory bought during inflation, and inflation lifts sales as deflation or tariff reversals would lower them. Management says over three-quarters of purchased products are made in the United States, which limits tariff exposure, and petroleum costs affect delivery. Revenue is therefore cyclical and construction-linked, not predictable; for creditors a volume decline reaches EBITDA quickly because nothing is contracted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gross profit was 26.61% of net sales in fiscal 2024 against 27.13% in fiscal 2023, and 26.95% in the first half of fiscal 2026 against 26.72%, a band of about half a percentage point that management attributes to purchasing, pricing and private label work. Costs below gross profit are sticky: in fiscal 2024 SG&A rose 15.79% against net sales growth of 11.03%, operating income fell 2.84% and the Adjusted EBITDA margin fell from 13.58% to 12.50%; in the first half of fiscal 2026 SG&A was 14.8% of net sales and the margin was 12.33% against 12.24%.

fields.value: Each 1 percentage point of gross margin is USD 40.55 million of six-month gross profit, 8.11% of six-month Adjusted EBITDA, and each 1% fall in six-month sales removes USD 10.93 million, 2.19% of that EBITDA, if SG&A does not fall. Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure because gross margin has moved little, but not against a deep volume fall unless SG&A is cut, and the quarterly report mentions cost actions without amounts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital expenditure was 0.47% of net sales in fiscal 2024 and 0.79% in the first half of fiscal 2026, with no split between maintenance and growth. Operating cash flow was 117.47% of Adjusted EBITDA in fiscal 2023, 66.77% in fiscal 2024 and 28.80% in the first half of fiscal 2026 against 22.65%, because working capital absorbed USD 242 million in the latest half and USD 255 million a year earlier; the company says operating cash flow is typically lower in the first two quarters and higher in the last two. Free cash flow was USD 1,030 million in fiscal 2023, USD 586 million in fiscal 2024 and USD 112 million in the latest half against USD 88 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash taxes of USD 40 million and cash interest of USD 59 million were paid in the latest half before free cash flow, and operating lease liabilities of USD 300 million sit outside debt. EBITDA converts into durable free cash flow over a full year on the evidence of fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2024, with the first half funded by the revolver and cash; the fiscal 2026 outlook of operating cash flow at 60% to 70% of Adjusted EBITDA implies second-half operating cash flow of USD 426 million to USD 542 million, and capex flexibility is high because spending is small.

fields.value: Basis: calculation OC1; calculation GL6; calculation GL7; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8; EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is moderate: the company faces one other national distributor and hundreds of regional and local ones, and it competes on availability, local expertise and project planning as well as price, which fits a gross margin that has stayed within about half a percentage point; a price war would show first in that margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation GM1; calculation GM2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of new entrants is low to moderate: a national branch network, supplier distribution rights and local specification knowledge take time to build, although the company itself opens greenfield locations, so regional entry is feasible; entry would pressure local gross margin rather than refinancing capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of substitutes is moderate: the company lists the development of alternatives to distributors, including direct sales by suppliers to end users, among its risks; substitution would reduce volume and sticky SG&A would turn it into EBITDA loss.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is low per customer, because the largest customer is under 1% of net sales, but municipal bidding and contractor price sensitivity limit price increases, which supports stable revenue and a limited ability to widen margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier power is moderate: the largest supplier is about 7% and the top ten about 43% of product expenditures, suppliers pay rebates for volume, and cost increases are passed on with a lag; supply disruption or tariff changes would hit gross margin before prices catch up.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulatory funding and the economic cycle are material to credit quality; social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials. The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act includes USD 55 billion for water infrastructure, most of which management believes has yet to be spent, and a January 2025 order paused some disbursements without affecting water or road projects; a lasting cut would lower municipal demand, 42% of sales on management's estimate. Interest rates and housing and commercial construction drive private demand and the variable-rate cost of USD 1,728 million of debt, and tariffs and petroleum prices affect product and delivery costs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: customer diversification, liquidity of USD 1,538 million, no maturity before 2031 and a gross margin steady near 27%. Weaknesses: shareholder returns above free cash flow, sticky SG&A, USD 685 million of tax receivable claims and flat EBITDA over three years. Opportunities: municipal and fire protection demand and acquisitions, which would raise credit quality only if funded from cash flow. Threats: a construction downturn, deflation or tariff reversals in product prices, higher rates after the swap ends in July 2028, and a larger debt-funded acquisition or buyback.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation LQ1; calculation OC2; calculation GM1; calculation GM2; calculation GM3; calculation GM4; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 97; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 27, 28; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest support is liquidity and maturity profile: USD 1,538 million of liquidity on an undrawn revolver and a first final maturity in February 2031 mean that seasonal working capital and debt service can be met without market access for several years, so refinancing risk is low before fiscal 2030.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation LQ1; calculation LQ5; calculation DS5; calculation DS6; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 19, 36; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second support is a broad customer base with low capital needs: no customer is above 1% of net sales, the top 50 are about 10% and capital expenditure is 0.47% of net sales, so cash flow does not depend on a single account or on heavy reinvestment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third support is a stable gross margin of 26.61% to 27.13% across periods, which together with pass-through pricing limits margin shocks from supplier cost changes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation GM1; calculation GM2; calculation GM3; calculation GM4; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth support is demonstrated market access on improving terms: three term loan repricings since May 2024 and a July 2026 refinancing that raised USD 1,550 million of new debt, with fair values of 99.60% of par for the notes, 99.75% for the 2033 loan and 100.00% for the 2031 loan.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation RF1; calculation DS14; calculation DS15; calculation DS16; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 17, 18; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth support is the absence of a controlling holder, a dividend or a creditor-adverse transaction in the documents supplied, which removes sponsor extraction as a driver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main weakness is financial policy: USD 299 million of repurchases and tax receivable payments in the first half of fiscal 2026 exceeded free cash flow of USD 112 million by USD 187 million and net new debt was USD 293 million, so leverage rises unless EBITDA grows or repurchases slow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation SR1; calculation FC4; calculation SR2; calculation SR3; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 8; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is that leverage is not measurable on a trailing basis and has risen: net debt to reported EBITDA went from 2.11x to 2.49x in fiscal 2024 and cash interest cover from 8.47x to 4.59x, and no later ratio is stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation LV1; calculation LV2; calculation CV1; calculation CV2; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third weakness is operating leverage in a construction-linked business: SG&A grew 15.79% against sales growth of 11.03% in fiscal 2024 and Adjusted EBITDA has been flat since fiscal 2022, so a volume decline would reach cash flow faster than costs fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation GR1; calculation GR3; calculation EB1; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 86, 97

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth weakness is claims outside debt: USD 985 million of lease liabilities and tax receivable payable, 46.09% of net debt, with the tax receivable payable accelerating on a change of control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation OC1; calculation OC2; calculation OC3; calculation OC4; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth weakness is rate exposure: 69.73% of principal is variable-rate, the swap covers 86.81% of it only to July 2028, and each 1 percentage point on all variable-rate debt would cost USD 17.28 million a year after that.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation DS7; calculation DS8; calculation DS9; calculation DS12; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The nine dimensions are assessed as follows, each on the evidence cited.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Scale and market position: Strong. Net sales of USD 7,441 million in fiscal 2024 are 19.08% of the market management estimates, with one other national competitor, which gives scale in purchasing and branch coverage and cushions shocks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Competitive advantage: Average. Scale, local specification knowledge and supplier distribution rights are advantages that management describes, but a gross margin of 26.61% and Adjusted EBITDA margins of 12.50% to 13.58% show limited pricing power.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 15; calculation GM2; calculation EM1; calculation EM2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Business diversification: Average. Customers are broad (largest under 1%) and products numerous, but 67% of sales are pipes, valves and fittings, about 58% of sales are private construction and sales are in the United States and Canada only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cost and capex flexibility: Average. Capital expenditure is 0.47% of net sales and can be cut, but SG&A is sticky: it grew 15.79% in fiscal 2024 against sales growth of 11.03%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CX1; calculation GR1; calculation GR3; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 86, 108

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margin stability: Average. Gross margin moved within about half a percentage point but the Adjusted EBITDA margin fell from 13.58% to 12.50% in fiscal 2024 and is 12.33% in the latest half.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation GM1; calculation GM2; calculation EM1; calculation EM2; calculation EM4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Free cash flow stability: Average. Free cash flow was USD 1,030 million in fiscal 2023 and USD 586 million in fiscal 2024, with operating cash flow at 117.47% and 66.77% of Adjusted EBITDA, so conversion is seasonal and uneven; after shareholder returns the latest half was USD 187 million negative.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation FC1; calculation FC2; calculation CN1; calculation CN2; calculation SR2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ability to refinance and access capital markets: Strong. The July 2026 refinancing raised USD 1,550 million of new debt, with a notes fair value of 99.60% of par, repricings cut margins, and no maturity falls before 2031; no rating or spread is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation RF1; calculation DS14; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity position: Strong. Liquidity is USD 1,538 million, 6.36x the first-half working capital outflow, on an undrawn revolver whose availability depends on a borrowing base that is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation LQ1; calculation LQ5; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 36

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy and governance: Average. No controlling holder and no dividend are positives, while buybacks and tax receivable payments above free cash flow, USD 685 million of tax receivable claims and a Medium risk level in Business & governance are negatives.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation OC2; calculation SR1; calculation FC4; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit supports are liquidity, the maturity profile and customer breadth; the main constraints are financial policy, sticky SG&A and the unmeasurable trailing leverage. The trend is stable operations with rising absolute debt, from net debt of USD 1,877 million at the end of fiscal 2023 to USD 2,137 million at August 2, 2026 (USD 2,148 million pro forma for USD 11 million of repurchases after that date), and the missing datapoints are fiscal 2025 EBITDA and cash interest, covenant calculations, the borrowing base and any rating.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation ND1; calculation ND4; calculation PF1; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In the short term, 12 to 24 months, the only outlook the company gives is for fiscal 2026: net sales of USD 7,800 million to USD 7,900 million, Adjusted EBITDA of USD 950 million to USD 980 million (2.15% to 5.38% above fiscal 2024), a margin of 12.2% to 12.4% and operating cash flow at 60% to 70% of Adjusted EBITDA, and it reaffirmed this in September 2026. On the pro forma net debt of USD 2,148 million that is 2.19x to 2.26x, an indicator that supports the stable view if second-half cash flow of USD 426 million to USD 542 million arrives and buybacks stay near the first-half pace, but it is management's guidance, not an audited result.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation GL1; calculation GL3; calculation GL6; calculation GL7; calculation GL8; calculation GL9; calculation PF1; EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 5; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the debt moves toward its first final maturities, the 2031 loan in February 2031 and the revolver in April 2031; the interest rate swap ends in July 2028, which leaves all USD 1,728 million of variable-rate debt unhedged, and tax receivable payments rise as exchanges continue (USD 41 million expected within 12 months against USD 42 million paid in the first half). Tailwinds are municipal demand and federal water funding, fire protection growth of 15.3% in the first half, and management's acquisition pipeline; headwinds are storm drainage volume down 2.9%, flat first-quarter sales on lower volume, tariff and petroleum cost uncertainty, and higher rates if the housing and commercial cycle weakens. Company-specific pressure comes from the repurchase pace, with USD 412 million of authorization left, which would add debt if free cash flow does not cover it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation DS7; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 81; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 20, 27, 28, 31, 33; EX99.1_2026-05-03_cnm_cnmq12026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a downturn in private construction, which is about 58% of sales on management's estimates, coinciding with higher interest rates. The first operational break is volume: the first quarter of fiscal 2026 was flat on lower volume, storm drainage already fell 2.9% in the first half, and fire protection fell 13.37% in fiscal 2024. Revenue falls and margins follow because SG&A is sticky: each 1% fall in six-month sales removes USD 10.93 million of gross profit, and each point of gross margin lost is USD 40.55 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation NM1; calculation GR5; calculation SN1; calculation SN3; 10-K_2025-02-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 31, 33; EX99.1_2026-05-03_cnm_cnmq12026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow weakens, but the first-half working capital build of USD 242 million would shrink as receivables and inventory fall, which cushions cash; the borrowing base also shrinks with them, so availability under the USD 1,250 million revolver would fall by an amount that is not supplied. Liquidity of USD 1,538 million and near-term fixed claims of USD 58 million mean liquidity distress is unlikely in this scenario within a year; the exposure is leverage, because net debt of USD 2,148 million would sit on lower EBITDA and shareholder returns of USD 299 million in a half, if continued, add debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation WC1; calculation LQ1; calculation LQ3; calculation PF1; calculation SR1; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 18, 36; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management has levers: buybacks, acquisitions and greenfield openings are discretionary, capital expenditure is small, and tax receivable payments are contractual but linked to taxable income. The refinancing consequence is limited before fiscal 2030 because the first maturity is February 2031, and the variable-rate cost rises by USD 17.28 million a year per percentage point once the swap ends in July 2028. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress; whether leverage stays acceptable depends on whether buybacks are cut in time, and the observable triggers are in the monitoring table.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation DS12; 10-Q_2026-08-02_cnm.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 28; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Core & Main presents an adequate business profile supported by customer diversification, low capital needs and USD 1,538 million of liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by shareholder returns above free cash flow, USD 685 million of tax receivable claims and a leverage measure that can be fixed only to fiscal 2024. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because operating cash flow was 117.47% and 66.77% of Adjusted EBITDA in the last two fiscal years, although the first half is seasonally weak. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the leverage trend ahead of fiscal 2030, since no maturity falls before February 2031. The primary downside path is a construction downturn met with unchanged shareholder returns, which would raise leverage while liquidity holds. Against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector the business profile cannot be compared, because no peer data is supplied. Further analysis would require the annual report for fiscal 2025, the third-quarter report, the credit agreements and a rating or peer set. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: debt-funded shareholder returns ahead of a construction downturn.

The exhibit list of the second-quarter report dates a Seventh Amendment to the term loan credit agreement August 11, 2026, and Financial foundation records that date; the report itself does not label the amendment as the repricing, so the day is stated here as the amendment's date and not as an established repricing date.

Net debt, principal, liquidity and repurchase figures agree across the earlier modules and the sources.

fields.value: - High severity: The annual report for the year ended February 1, 2026 is not supplied, so fiscal 2025 EBITDA, cash interest and operating cash flow are missing and no trailing leverage or cover can be stated; leverage is shown at fiscal 2024 and as an indicator on guidance. The action that would close it is that annual report or the third-quarter report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium severity: The credit agreements, the borrowing base and the compliance certificates are not supplied, so covenant headroom, the revolver's true availability in a downturn and restricted-payment capacity are not measured. The action that would close it is the executed agreements and certificates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium severity: No credit rating, market spread or peer set is supplied, so the business and financial profile are not compared with other leveraged issuers and the notes' market pricing is known only through fair value at par. The action that would close it is rating reports and a peer benchmark.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low severity: The fiscal 2026 outlook is management's guidance and gives no capital expenditure or interest guidance, so free cash flow and net debt at the fiscal year end cannot be projected from it; the implied second-half operating cash flow is arithmetic on guidance. The action that would close it is the third-quarter report.

fields.value: Basis: EX99.1_2026-08-02_cnm_cnmq22026earningspressrele-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation GL6; calculation GL7

fields.value: - Low severity: The end-market split is a fiscal 2024 management estimate and the product category was renamed in 2026, and no contract length, renewal or churn data is supplied, so revenue durability is judged on customer breadth and category history. The action that would close it is the fiscal 2025 annual report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low severity: Maintenance and growth capital expenditure and the cost of the cost actions are not disclosed, so cost and capex flexibility is judged on total spending and the SG&A trend. No action closes this from the issuer's public statements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low severity: The latest supplied document is dated 2026-09-09, 70 days before the as-of date of 2026-11-18, and no third-quarter material is supplied; nothing after that document is used as fact. The action that would close it is the third-quarter report.

fields.value: The orchestrator selects the next module.
